subject: Urgent: Reset Your Password
content: Your Loyola account has been flagged for suspicious activity. Click the link below immediately to verify your password or your account will be locked.
feedback: This is phishing because it uses urgency and a suspicious sender address that does not match Loyola's official domain.
hint: Look closely at the sender domain and the urgent language asking you to act immediately.

subject: Scheduled Maintenance Notice
content: Loyola University Chicago IT will perform scheduled maintenance on student systems tonight from 11:00 PM to 1:00 AM. During this time, some services may be temporarily unavailable.
feedback: This message appears legitimate because it uses an official Loyola domain, gives informational details, and does not pressure the user to click suspicious links or share sensitive information.
hint: Check whether the sender uses an official Loyola email domain and whether the message is informational instead of urgent.

subject: School Email Verification / Suspension Warning
content: This is Karen Giblin from the Loyola University Newyork IT Help Center. We recently received a notification indicating that you are no longer a student at Loyola University school. ([LUCid]]@luc.edu) To proceed with the permanent deletion of your account, please confirm your decision by replying with YES to approve or NO to decline. We need to complete your school email account verification process to avoid your account from being suspended. Hello should we go ahead and suspend your school email account for now?
feedback: This is phishing because it comes from an unknown phone number, uses pressure and threats about deleting or suspending the account, contains awkward wording, and refers to a suspiciously named 'Loyola University Newyork IT Help Center' rather than an official Loyola contact.
hint: Notice the unknown phone number, the urgent threat about account suspension, and the unusual wording and naming of the supposed IT department.

subject: LOCUS Parent Guest Account Password Update Required by June 1, 2026
content:
Dear Student,

To keep accounts secure and meet updated University password standards, all Parent Guest Account passwords in LOCUS must be updated by June 1, 2026.

Parent Guest Accounts are managed by students, so you are responsible for updating the password and notifying your parents of the change.

If the password is not updated by the deadline, the University will automatically reset the Parent Guest Account password using a secure algorithm, which may cause temporary access issues.

If you need assistance, visit the Knowledge Base or contact the ITS Help Desk at ITSservicedesk@LUC.edu.

Sincerely,

Jim Pardonek
Chief Information Security Officer
feedback: This message appears legitimate because it uses an official Loyola email address, refers to a real university system, explains the policy clearly, and does not ask the user to click a suspicious link or provide sensitive information through an unofficial channel.
hint: Check whether the sender uses an official Loyola domain, whether the message gives realistic institutional instructions, and whether it avoids suspicious links or requests for personal information.

subject: USPS Package Delivery Issue
content:
URGENT NOTICE

Package delivery issue. Check attachment immediately to avoid package being returned.

XTRGU

Attachment: MODIFIED_usa32aigawau21_us.pdf
feedback: This is phishing because it comes from an unknown phone number, uses urgent pressure tactics, includes a suspicious random code, and sends an unexpected attachment. Legitimate delivery companies typically use official branded communication channels and do not send random PDF files by text.
hint: Look for urgency, unexpected attachments, random wording, and whether the sender is an official USPS contact.

subject: Illinois DMV Warning
content: ILLINOIS DMV WARNING: Time-sensitive traffic citation must be resolved by 03/17/26. Avoid permanent record, registration cancellation, 30-day suspension, and 35% penalty increase. Act officially: https://ilsos.org-npm.life/dmv
feedback: This is phishing because it uses fear and urgency about penalties, comes from an unknown phone number, and includes a suspicious link that imitates an Illinois government domain. Official DMV or Secretary of State notices typically use trusted government websites, not misleading domains.
hint: Check whether the sender is official, whether the message pressures you with threats, and whether the website domain truly matches a real government site.

subject: Immediate Action Required: Debit Card Frozen
content: Your debit card has been frozen due to suspicious transactions. Verify your identity within 30 minutes or your account will remain LOCKED.
feedback: This is phishing because it uses panic and urgency, threatens account lockout, and uses a suspicious sender domain that does not match a real bank.
hint: Check for urgent deadlines and whether the sender domain looks official.

subject: Unpaid Toll Violation
content: FINAL NOTICE: You owe unpaid toll charges. Pay today or face additional fines and vehicle registration suspension.
feedback: This is phishing because it uses fear tactics, urgency, and comes from an unknown number instead of an official toll authority.
hint: Look for threats, urgency, and unofficial sender identity.

subject: Payment Failed - Account Deletion Pending
content: Your payment failed and your streaming account will be permanently deleted tonight unless billing information is updated immediately.
feedback: This is phishing because it pressures the user into acting fast and uses a suspicious sender domain.
hint: Notice emotional pressure and the unofficial email address.

subject: Unauthorized Purchase Detected
content: We detected a $1,247 purchase on your PayPal account. If this was not you, confirm cancellation immediately through the secure portal below.
feedback: This is phishing because it creates panic about a fake charge and uses a suspicious sender domain pretending to be PayPal.
hint: Look at the sender carefully and notice how the fake charge is meant to scare you.

subject: IRS Tax Warrant Notice
content: IRS ALERT: Failure to respond to your overdue tax notice may result in wage garnishment or legal enforcement. Resolve today.
feedback: This is phishing because it impersonates the IRS through text, uses fear about legal action, and pressures immediate response.
hint: Government agencies rarely send threats like this through random texts.

subject: Student Account Suspension Warning
content: Your Loyola student account will be suspended today due to abnormal login attempts. Confirm your identity now to avoid losing email access.
feedback: This is phishing because it imitates a school IT message, uses fear of losing access, and uses a fake Loyola-related domain.
hint: Look closely at the domain name and urgency.

subject: Large Wire Transfer Pending
content: A $9,850 wire transfer request is pending on your Chase account. If you did not authorize this request, verify cancellation immediately.
feedback: This is phishing because the sender domain only appears to be Chase. The extra domain ending shows it is fake and the large dollar amount is meant to cause panic.
hint: Read the full domain carefully, especially what comes after the real brand name.

subject: Family Emergency Contact
content: Mom was taken to the hospital. Doctors need immediate family authorization. Call me now and verify your information.
feedback: This is phishing because it exploits fear and family panic while requesting immediate contact and personal verification from an unknown number.
hint: Emotional emergencies are common scam tactics when sent from unknown contacts.

subject: Suspicious Order Shipped
content: Your order for Apple MacBook Pro has shipped to an unrecognized address. If fraudulent, cancel within 15 minutes before final processing.
feedback: This is phishing because it creates panic over an expensive fake purchase and uses a deceptive domain pretending to be Amazon.
hint: The brand name appears in the sender, but check the full domain ending.

subject: Hospital Emergency Contact
content: This is Advocate Hospital. Your father listed you as emergency contact and cannot speak. We need identity confirmation and insurance details immediately.
feedback: This is phishing because it exploits fear involving family emergencies while requesting personal information from an unknown number.
hint: Emotional urgency involving family is a common social engineering tactic.

subject: Service Suspension Scheduled Today
content: Your internet service is scheduled for suspension today due to a failed autopay charge. To avoid interruption during finals week, re-confirm your billing details now.
feedback: This is phishing because it targets a stressful time, uses fear of losing service, and uses a deceptive sender domain pretending to be Xfinity.
hint: Notice how the sender contains the brand name but ends in a different domain.

subject: Federal Return Flagged for Identity Conflict
content: Your federal tax return was flagged because another filing used your Social Security Number. Immediate identity confirmation is required to prevent refund seizure.
feedback: This is phishing because it weaponizes identity theft fears and uses a fake sender that only imitates a government domain.
hint: Government names in the sender do not guarantee legitimacy. Check the full domain ending.
